# NSSFactory r4 — Sirius

_The brightest one is close by._

r4 optimizes every filter not yet on Vulkan and freezes its model, adds WNNM and MCWNNM to `nss_vk`, runs `nss_vk` on devices with 32 KiB of shared memory, and takes VapourSynth GPU frames without switches or core checks.

**Work in progress.** The packages below are preview builds for evaluation, not stable releases. `nss_vk` is a further preview: NLM, BM3D, PNLM, WNNM and MCWNNM are ported, and it is validated on NVIDIA GPUs only.

## Packages

| Package | Plugin | Runs on |
|---|---|---|
| `nssfactory-r4-linux-x86_64.tar.gz` | `libnss.so` (`nss`) | x86-64 with AVX2; glibc 2.34 and the libstdc++ of GCC 13 (Ubuntu 24.04, Debian 13, Fedora 39 or later). Highway dynamic: AVX2 + AVX3/Zen4 |
| `nssfactory-r4-linux-arm64.tar.gz` | `libnss.so` (`nss`) | AArch64 with glibc 2.38 (libstdc++ built in). NEON |
| `nssfactory-r4-macos-arm64.tar.gz` | `libnss.dylib` (`nss`) | Apple silicon, macOS 13.3 or newer. NEON |
| `nssfactory-r4-windows-x86_64.zip` | `libnss.dll` (`nss`) | x86-64 with AVX2 and the Visual C++ 2015–2022 Redistributable |
| `nssfactory-r4-linux-x86_64-cuda.tar.gz` | `libnss_cuda.so` (`nss_cuda`) | as `linux-x86_64`, with an NVIDIA driver r580 or newer (CUDA 13) |
| `nssfactory-r4-windows-x86_64-cuda.zip` | `libnss_cuda.dll` (`nss_cuda`) | an NVIDIA driver r580 or newer (CUDA 13) and the Visual C++ Redistributable |
| `nssfactory-r4-linux-x86_64-vk.tar.gz` | `libnss_vk.so` (`nss_vk`) | a Vulkan 1.3 device with the features in the [Vulkan reference](https://github.com/AmusementClub/vapoursynth-nssfactory/blob/master/docs/api/vk/README.md); NVIDIA validated, AMD and Intel untested |
| `nssfactory-r4-windows-x86_64-vk.zip` | `libnss_vk.dll` (`nss_vk`) | a Vulkan 1.3 device with the features in the [Vulkan reference](https://github.com/AmusementClub/vapoursynth-nssfactory/blob/master/docs/api/vk/README.md); NVIDIA validated, AMD and Intel untested |

Clips must be constant-format Gray/YUV/RGB 32-bit float. Each package carries `docs/api`: the [API guide](https://github.com/AmusementClub/vapoursynth-nssfactory/blob/master/docs/api/README.md), the [CUDA reference](https://github.com/AmusementClub/vapoursynth-nssfactory/blob/master/docs/api/cuda/README.md), the [Vulkan reference](https://github.com/AmusementClub/vapoursynth-nssfactory/blob/master/docs/api/vk/README.md) and the [comparison with other plugins](https://github.com/AmusementClub/vapoursynth-nssfactory/blob/master/docs/api/cuda/compare.md). `core.nss.Version()`, `core.nss_cuda.Version()` and `core.nss_vk.Version()` report `r4`.

## Highlights

- **Every filter optimized, then frozen.** WNNM, NCSR, MCWNNM, TWSC, NLH, LSSC, DA3D and BM4D each had a round on CUDA and on the CPU, and their models are now frozen, so the Vulkan ports that follow take finished models. No model version changes. On `nss_cuda` (1080p YUV420, RTX 5080, GPU frames), each step timed in pairs against the code before it:
  - WNNM heavy 2.2x (groups of 17 to 32 by divide and conquer), MCWNNM heavy 1.9x, NCSR heavy 1.2x;
  - TWSC 1.2x at its defaults and 1.3x heavy, NLH 1.14 to 1.2x, LSSC 1.2x;
  - BM4D 1.3x, DA3D 1.1x (RGB 1.2x).
- **Faster on the CPU:** the Jacobi SVD of WNNM's, NCSR's and MCWNNM's groups above 8 is vectorized (heavy settings 1.25 to 1.7x); BM4D 3.4x; DA3D 1.2x; TWSC, NLH and LSSC 1.1 to 1.2x. BM3D and WNNM share their matching work at `block_step=4` with groups of 16 or more (BM3D 1.24 to 1.29x on x86, 1.09x on NEON; the defaults are unchanged).
- **New in `nss_vk`: WNNM and MCWNNM** (spatial and temporal), with the arguments and defaults of `nss` and `nss_cuda`. At the defaults on GPU frames WNNM runs at about 1340 fps (0.95 times `nss_cuda`) and MCWNNM at 310 on RGB (1.2 times). `nss_vk` now also picks its own kernel paths where Vulkan measures faster than CUDA's: PNLM's defaults 1.18x, BM3D's 16/16 Wiener stage 1.22 to 1.28x.
- **`nss_vk` on devices with 32 KiB of shared memory** (current AMD drivers on Windows, AMDVLK, Intel GPUs on Windows): the kernels that needed more fall back to smaller variants there. These devices remain untested, as AMD and Intel do in general.
- **GPU frames without switches or core checks.** `nss_cuda` takes GPU frames on VapourSynth R81 and every later core, `nss_vk` on R80 and later; neither downloads GPU clips on cores newer than the ones it was tested on, and the environment switches that turned GPU frames off (`NSS_CUDA_GPU_FRAMES`, `NSS_VK_GPU_FRAMES`) are gone. A source build of `nss_cuda` has GPU frames whenever it is built against R81 or newer headers ([GPU frames](https://github.com/AmusementClub/vapoursynth-nssfactory/blob/master/docs/api/cuda/README.md#gpu-frames)).

## Fixes

- DA3D rejects planes smaller than 2 x 2 (a plane of one row, such as the chroma of a two-row 4:2:0 clip, never finished).

## Upgrading from r3

- **No model version changes:** legacy temporal intermediates of r3 stay valid for `VAggregate`. Outputs can still move in the last bits: `nss_cuda` WNNM groups of 17 to 32 and BM4D's denominators, and the CPU's vectorized SVD and its square matcher (BM3D and WNNM, `block_step=4`, groups of 16 or more), all checked against PSNR gates.
- **`NSS_CUDA_GPU_FRAMES` and `NSS_VK_GPU_FRAMES` are removed.** To run a filter on CPU frames on R80 and later, give it a CPU clip (`std.GPUDownload`).
- **Source builds:** the CMake option `NSS_CUDA_GPU_FRAMES` is removed; GPU frames follow the VapourSynth headers, as `nss_vk`'s already did.

## Known limits

- `nss_vk` is a preview: NLM, BM3D, PNLM, WNNM and MCWNNM are ported, and it is validated on NVIDIA GPUs only; AMD and Intel GPUs are untested.
- `nss_cuda` GPU frames and the direct transfers with vapoursynth-classic are validated on Linux (RTX 5080); on Windows they are build-tested only.
- PNLM, BM4D and DA3D take the noise's true sigma and assume white Gaussian noise.
- Speeds are measured on one RTX 5080 with a Ryzen 9 5950X; other GPUs are untested for speed.
- NLH's blind estimate still reads textured luma high at very low noise (sigma 5 or less); give `sigma` there when it is known.
